findings.design: A standalone full-page screen at route /admin/certifications/:code/re-verify — own AdminSidebar, own header, occupies the whole viewport for one certification's stale-metadata review.
findings.app: No such route exists (Glob of apps/web/app/pages/admin/certifications only returns index.vue and new.vue). The reverify flow is an inline card that expands at the bottom of the generic /admin/certifications list page after clicking a table row's 'Re-verify' button — there is no per-cert navigation/URL.

findings.element: Stale-cert header (breadcrumb + cert title + 'Metadata stale · action required' pill)
findings.design: Page header shows breadcrumb 'Certifications › SAA-C03 › Re-verification required' (last crumb in warning color), the cert's display name 'Solutions Architect – Associate' as an H1-equivalent, and a right-aligned warning-colored pill 'Metadata stale · action required'.
findings.app: No per-cert header is rendered for the reverify state; the page still shows the generic 'Certifications' h1 (shared with the rest of the list page). No breadcrumb and no stale-status pill exist anywhere in the component.

findings.element: Stale-reason callout ('Exam guide updated — November 2024' explanation)
findings.design: A warning-tinted callout with icon explains *why* re-verification is needed: 'AWS published a revised SAA-C03 exam guide. The agent identified changes to domain weightings and 2 renamed domains.'
findings.app: No explanatory callout is rendered anywhere in the reverify flow — the admin sees only the raw diff table with no narrative context for the change.

findings.element: Per-row 'Accept' button for individually changed fields
findings.design: Each DiffRow shows an individual 'Accept' button only for rows that changed, letting the admin accept field changes one at a time.
findings.app: Only a single bulk 'Accept all & re-verify' button exists for the whole diff; there is no per-row accept control or ability to selectively accept individual field changes.
findings.evidence: design: openspec/design/AdminCertSetup.html:504-513 (DiffRow's conditional Accept button); app: apps/web/app/components/admin/AdminCertifications.vue:265-296 (no per-row action column)

findings.element: Domain-level diff granularity + Validity period / Exam version rows
findings.design: Diff table has 8 granular rows: Domain 1 name, Domain 1 weight, Domain 3 name, Domain 3 weight, Domain 4 weight, Validity period, Exam version, Passing score — each domain's name and weight independently comparable.
findings.app: All domains are collapsed into a single 'Domains' row formatted as a comma-joined string (e.g. 'Name (30%), ...'); there is no per-domain name/weight comparison. 'Validity period' and 'Exam version' fields don't exist in the reverify schema at all (CertProposedValues only has domains, questionCount, passingScore, timeLimitMinutes).

findings.element: Changed-value color coding (strikethrough red old / bold green new)
findings.design: Changed rows render the old value with strikethrough + red (poor) text on a faint red background, and the new value bold + green (good) text on a faint green background; unchanged rows are muted/subtle in both columns.
findings.app: The 'current' cell is always plain slate-300 text with no strikethrough or red tint. The 'proposed' cell only gets a color change (readion-primary) when changed — no strikethrough, no distinct background tinting for changed vs. unchanged rows.

findings.element: Footer actions: 'Review source URL first' / 'Accept all changes' / 'Save & mark verified'
findings.design: Three distinct actions: a left-anchored secondary 'Review source URL first' (lets the admin verify the source before trusting the diff), and a right-side pair — secondary 'Accept all changes' and primary 'Save & mark verified' — implying accept-then-commit as two steps.
findings.app: Only two actions exist: 'Accept all & re-verify' (primary, submits immediately) and 'Cancel'. There is no source-URL review action and no separation between accepting changes and committing/marking verified — it's a single combined submit.

findings.element: Full-height split-panel layout vs. boxed inline section
findings.design: Edge-to-edge flex layout: fixed-width AdminSidebar plus a flex-1 content column that fills the viewport height, dedicated entirely to this one certification's re-verification.
findings.app: AdminConsole renders a centered `mx-auto max-w-7xl` boxed container shared by the whole /admin/certifications page; the reverify diff appears as one more card stacked beneath two other tables (existing certs, due-for-reverification), not as a focused full-height screen.

findings.element: Diff section label & colored column headers ('Field changes detected' / 'Current (outdated)' / 'Proposed (new guide)')
findings.design: Uppercase eyebrow label 'Field changes detected' above the table; column headers explicitly read 'Current (outdated)' (red) and 'Proposed (new guide)' (green).
findings.app: Section is titled 'Proposed changes' (h2, not an uppercase eyebrow) with plain, uncolored column headers 'Current' and 'Proposed'.

findings.design: The stale-diff screen has no unverified-field annotation — that status concept belongs to the separate field-extraction screen (StatusBadge), not the re-verification diff.
findings.app: Adds a '(unverified)' text annotation next to the field label when the extracted value lacks a citation, a behavior not present in the corresponding design screen.
findings.evidence: design: openspec/design/AdminCertSetup.html:504-513 (no such annotation in DiffRow); app: apps/web/app/components/admin/AdminCertifications.vue:274

reconciliation.snapshotPolicy: Claude HTML remains visual hierarchy evidence; implemented live, accessible, theme, and responsive behavior is the product contract where static frames cannot demonstrate it.

statusVocabulary.resolved: implementation now matches the cited snapshot evidence

intentionalProductContracts.colorModes: Dark and light modes use semantic Readion tokens and meet 4.5:1 normal-text and 3:1 large-text/non-text minimum contrast.
intentionalProductContracts.controls: Controls expose rest, hover, active, focus-visible, disabled, selected, and action-local busy states with stable dimensions, reduced-motion handling, semantic state, duplicate guards, and operation-specific labels.
intentionalProductContracts.async: HTTP regions distinguish initial loading, content, successful empty, error with Retry, and content-preserving background refresh.
intentionalProductContracts.accessibility: Progress and outcomes are announced; modal focus enters a meaningful control, traps traversal, supports permitted Escape/backdrop dismissal, and returns to the opener.
intentionalProductContracts.responsive: Implemented shell screens contain content at 375px with wrapping or bounded local overflow while preserving the desktop artboard hierarchy.
